query: How can sellers improve Amazon product satisfaction?

per_column.name: content_or_media_quality
per_column.rationale: Categorizing WHY media content is weak or strong gives sellers/analysts an actionable axis for improving satisfaction on media products, and 'not_applicable' correctly handles physical-product rows. Values are largely sound readings: AMZ-0003 'appallingly shallow' -> content_shallow_or_thin, AMZ-0005 praise -> high_quality_content. The AMZ-0002 'pacing_poor' label is a slightly loose fit (the complaint is about too much political commentary, not pacing per se), a minor grounding stretch but not an invention.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: Product category is a strong grouping axis for the query: sellers can compare satisfaction drivers across books, music, DVDs, physical goods, etc. Values are well grounded in the text: baby doll -> physical_product_non_consumable, book review -> book_or_printed_media, music/artist -> music_cd_or_vinyl, Criterion film/DVD -> dvd_or_video. NULL used where category is unclear, which is appropriate. Well-warranted inferences throughout.

judge.rationale: Both added columns provide genuine, distinct analytical axes (product type and content-quality failure mode) directly relevant to how sellers can improve satisfaction, neither being near-constant nor a trivial restatement of the original title/content fields. Values are generally sound readings of the source text with reasonable use of not_applicable/NULL for silent rows; the only weak spot is a somewhat loose 'pacing_poor' label on AMZ-0002, which is a minor grounding imperfection rather than a fabricated fact.
